reports.title: Google DeepMind and Singapore Government collaborate to build fine-tuned AI model for scam detection
reports.summary: Learn how Google DeepMind and GovTech Singapore uses lightweight on-device Gemma models to intercept conversational scams in private chats with zero cloud data egress.

editorial.summary:
Google DeepMind reported that it is collaborating with the Singapore Government on a fine-tuned AI model aimed at detecting scams. According to the company, the work involves GovTech Singapore and uses lightweight Gemma models that run on-device to intercept conversational scams in private chats. The company said the approach keeps data off the cloud, with no data egress to cloud servers.

The only report in this coverage came from Google DeepMind itself, so the account reflects the company's own description of the project. No independent outlet's reporting is included here.
editorial.whyItMatters: The project shows frontier AI developers working with a government on targeted, privacy-focused tools against fraud. It is a narrow application of AI rather than a development toward more general capabilities.
keyFacts: Google DeepMind said it is collaborating with the Singapore Government on a fine-tuned AI model for scam detection.
The company named GovTech Singapore as a partner in the work.
According to Google DeepMind, the system uses lightweight on-device Gemma models to intercept conversational scams in private chats.
The company said the approach involves zero cloud data egress.
